twists.name: Harbor night shift
twists.summary: Port lighting and cold storage need more power, while the local power line can supply less.

twists.name: Heat wave
twists.summary: Homes use 60% more power for cooling. Plan for 48 hours of backup.

twists.name: Suspicious battery readings
twists.summary: Home 3 claims a full battery, but its report fails a security check. Leave it out of the plan until checked.

twists.name: Cell network outage
twists.summary: Homes 2 and 4 lose their connection. Their battery status is unknown, and the cell tower needs power right away.

demoScript.title: Ordinary Tuesday
demoScript.caption: These six example homes use real June 2024 electricity averages from LA ZIP codes. On a normal day, their batteries can sell spare energy when demand is high, while keeping backup power for each home.

demoScript.title: Helping the local power grid
demoScript.caption: The utility needs homes to draw less power. First, reduce usage where residents agree. Then use spare battery energy. Ask the utility for help with anything the plan cannot cover.

demoScript.title: Fire-weather warning
demoScript.caption: A fire-weather shutoff warning arrives (scenario; the bundled NWS snapshot is shown for context). Residents get a reviewed Prepare-now alert. Simulated outbox only, nothing is sent.

demoScript.title: Spread out charging before the outage
demoScript.caption: If everyone starts charging at 4 PM, they need more power than is available. PoweruP spreads charging across 18 hours, helping homes with the greatest need first.

demoScript.title: Dispatcher approves the budget
demoScript.caption: A human approves the plan. Only loads residents accepted can be reduced; essential loads are never touched. No real commands are sent.

demoScript.title: Outage hours 0–72
demoScript.caption: Power goes out at 6 PM. Each home gets a power-use plan aimed at keeping essential devices running for 72 hours. Homes without enough energy are flagged for help.

demoScript.title: 3 AM: connection loss
demoScript.caption: At 3 AM four batteries go quiet. They keep following the local plan they already have. PoweruP sorts them: not talking, breaker tripped, or broken, and stops counting them as verified capacity.

demoScript.title: Handoff to the operator
demoScript.caption: The operator sees who needs help: homes running short of energy, batteries that stopped reporting, and nearby services that cannot wait for power. Every decision is saved in the activity history.
